newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal says privatisation of telecoms on target.
newsitem.headline: Senegal says privatisation of telecoms on target.

text.p: Negotiations between Senegal and France Telecom over the privatisation of Senegalese state telephone company SONATEL will be completed soon, sources at the privatisation committee said on Wednesday.
"Things are moving in the right direction. I am confident it will be completed soon," one committee official told Reuters.

France Telecom started talks for the purchase of a one-third stake in SONATEL after Senegal's April 16 cancellation of a provisional deal worth 70 billion CFA francs ($118.6 million) with a consortium led by Swedish company Telia Overseas.
The Swedish group wanted a seven-year concession which would have lasted only until a proposed end of its monopoly over the fixed-line network.

"We have overcome one of the main problems we had with the Swedish-led consortium. France Telecom has agreed for a concession of 20 years and will enjoy a monopoly of seven years only over the fixed line (network)," the source added.
During the previous bid, France Telecom had made the second best offer of 65 billion CFA.
Senegal proposes selling the remaining two-thirds of SONATEL to private Senegalese and African investors.
Senegal's Telecoms workers union which recently complained of being completely left in the dark over the privatisation moves, last week met representatives of France Telecom.
Senegal plans to liberalise its cellular telephone sector next year, with January as the target date for the start of a second network.
SONATEL started the West African nation's first cellular telephone service in October, using a GSM system.
The state phone company has a capital of 50 billion CFA francs and an annual turnover of more than 60 billion CFA francs.
